newsitem.title: USA: Safety-Kleen down after profit warning.
newsitem.headline: Safety-Kleen down after profit warning.

text.p: Safety-Kleen Corp fell about 16 percent Wednesday after the company warned that first quarter profits would be lower than a year ago.

Late Tuesday, the Elgin, Illinois-based environmental and industrial service company said it expected first quarter earnings to be about $0.20 a share, down from $0.23 a share a year ago, due to pressure on lube oil selling prices.

"Most analysts weren't expecting much more than modest earnings growth this year anyhow because of the margin pressures in this (oil recovery) business," Michael Hutchison, analyst at Barrington Research said.
But he noted that the consensus estimate for the first quarter was $0.24 a share, so the earnings projection Tuesday was below consensus.

Hutchison said the oil recovery business accounted for about 16 percent of Safety-Kleen's revenue in the fourth quarter. He also noted that unlike the company's other businesses, the oil recovery line is more volatile.
"This oil recovery business is much more sensitive to prices and capacity than any of their other businesses," he said.
Safety-Kleen shares were down three at 15-3/8 Wednesday.
